questions.q: Which of these best defines AI governance as used in this course?
options: The system of decision rights, accountability, and controls over how data is sourced, models are built, and model decisions are owned
A single software tool that scans a model for bugs
The job title of one person responsible for AI ethics
A one-time checklist completed before a model launches
questions.explain: AI governance is an ongoing system of agreements and accountability, not a tool, one role, or a one-time checklist.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what are the three buckets AI governance is organized around?
options: The data going in, the model itself, and the decisions coming out
Marketing, sales, and finance
Hardware, software, and networking
Hiring, training, and firing
questions.explain: The lesson organizes AI governance — and much of this course — around data in, the model, and decisions out.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say AI governance is not a brand-new discipline for an organization that already runs data governance?
options: Because it extends the same decision-rights and accountability structure to cover a model's behavior and continuous automated decisions
Because AI governance requires no roles or policies at all
Because AI systems are not considered data by any organization
Because data governance teams are legally barred from touching AI
questions.explain: The lesson frames AI governance as an extension of existing data governance structures, not a separate discipline built from scratch.

questions.q: What specifically does data governance alone typically NOT fully reach, according to the lesson?
options: A trained model's learned behavior, and decisions made continuously without per-instance human review
Spreadsheets and databases
Any data stored in the cloud
Customer service phone calls
questions.explain: The lesson specifically calls out a model's learned behavior and continuous automated decisions as the new reach AI governance adds.

questions.q: Per the lesson's roadmap, what does Chapter 2 of this course focus on?
options: Governing the data that trains models
Writing production Python code
Mock job interviews
Building a company's marketing website
questions.explain: Chapter 2, "Data for AI," covers governing training data — provenance, consent, quality, bias, labeling, and synthetic data.
